lead_dispositions.researcher_interpretation: Hyperscaler/cloud infrastructure demand should be represented as linked but distinct signals: hyperscaler server/infrastructure procurement on one side and memory-supplier data-center/HBM/DIMM/SSD demand on the other.
lead_dispositions.canonical_boundary: Do not map hyperscaler capex dollars directly into DRAM/NAND/HBM bits, SSD units or supplier revenue without claim-scoped procurement evidence.

lead_dispositions.researcher_interpretation: Accelerator platform memory content can change materially across product generations; H200 provides a direct platform-specific HBM-capacity observation.
lead_dispositions.canonical_boundary: Do not infer a universal accelerator-memory growth rate or total HBM market demand from one platform comparison.

lead_dispositions.researcher_interpretation: AI accelerator effective supply can be constrained outside memory fabs. TSMC's July 2024 CoWoS statement establishes an external advanced-packaging constraint and forward capacity response.
lead_dispositions.canonical_boundary: Do not relabel CoWoS tightness as HBM shortage; current tightness and 2025 capacity guidance belong to different epistemic layers.

lead_dispositions.researcher_interpretation: Device memory demand must preserve both unit assumptions and content-per-device assumptions. Gartner supplied a contemporaneous unit-growth forecast while Micron separately forecast materially higher DRAM content for AI PCs and phones.
lead_dispositions.canonical_boundary: Do not multiply two forecasts into realized bit demand. Preserve forecast vintage, speaker and later Outcome separately.

lead_dispositions.researcher_interpretation: Enterprise/data-center SSD demand is not a sudden 2024 phenomenon; by 2024 primary sources show AI/hyperscale infrastructure demand and very high-density enterprise SSD products as a concrete continuation of prior NVMe/QLC scaling.
lead_dispositions.canonical_boundary: This packet does not establish the full 2019-2024 adoption chronology or customer qualification history.

lead_dispositions.researcher_interpretation: AI storage can raise capacity requirements faster than storage-device counts; the 61.44TB-to-122TB enterprise SSD step is a direct capacity-per-drive milestone relevant to NAND bit-demand analysis.
lead_dispositions.canonical_boundary: Do not infer aggregate exabytes shipped, SSD unit growth or AI-induced NAND demand magnitude from product capacity alone.

research_compositions.summary: Cloud/AI demand drives hyperscaler server/infrastructure procurement while memory suppliers report AI-led hyperscale SSD and high-value memory demand; the bridge is economically meaningful but not a deterministic capex-to-memory conversion.
Device bit demand should be reasoned as unit trajectory × content trajectory, with each input retaining its own forecast/Reality status and vintage.

Accelerator-system memory demand and availability span HBM content per accelerator, memory-fab silicon intensity, memory packaging/TSV, foundry advanced packaging and final platform demand; no single stage should be assumed binding without dated evidence.
Enterprise SSD capacity per device can grow sharply even without comparable SSD unit growth, so NAND demand analysis should prefer capacity/exabytes over unit counts where available.
